summaries.portfolio-react: Bilingual, server-rendered portfolio built with React 19, React Router 7, and TypeScript. Includes localized routes and metadata, a validated contact flow, security headers, and automated tests.
summaries.spacex-explorer: Native Android app that browses SpaceX launch, rocket, and crew data through the public v4 API, organized around Clean Architecture with Hilt-driven DI and Kotlin Coroutines.
summaries.sgci-app: .NET Core CLI business application that manages purchase workflows, stock, third-party relationships, promotional plans, cash registers, and customizable transactions.
summaries.campuslove: Matchmaking simulator backed by PostgreSQL. Users create profiles, browse a match feed, and interact through a modular architecture focused on persistence and data shape.
summaries.todo-list-flask: Flask task-management web app with user registration, login, and persistent per-user to-do lists backed by SQLite, deployed to PythonAnywhere.
summaries.formula1-webcomponents: Interactive Formula 1 management and 3D-simulation app. Manage teams, drivers, and vehicles, then run circuit simulations rendered with Three.js — all composed from native Web Components.

portfolio-react.text: This portfolio is a full-stack project built with React 19, React Router 7 server rendering, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. Feature-based modules and typed project data keep the content and page components organized.

items: English and Spanish routes, content, and metadata through i18next
Contact forms validated with Zod and React Hook Form, with honeypot and rate limiting protection
Server-side email delivery through Resend
CSP nonce headers and an /api/health endpoint
Vercel deployment support, Vitest unit tests, and Playwright browser tests

portfolio-react.text: I built the interface and the server-side contact flow, connecting form feedback, validation, email delivery, security headers, and deployment. The project includes unit tests and browser tests for the complete application.

spacex-explorer.text: SpaceX Explorer is a native Android app for exploring SpaceX data through its public v4 API. I built it with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, with Clean Architecture separating the interface, application logic, and data access.

items: Jetpack Compose for the Android interface
Clean Architecture to separate responsibilities
Hilt for dependency injection
Kotlin Coroutines for asynchronous API calls
Integration with the public SpaceX API v4

spacex-explorer.text: I built the Android interface and API integration, with separate layers for presentation, application logic, and data access.

sgci-app.text: SGCI is the project where I treated Clean Architecture as non-negotiable. The CLI is only the delivery mechanism — underneath, the domain layer models purchases, stock movements, promotional plans, and cash registers as aggregates with their own invariants. The application layer orchestrates use cases, and infrastructure adapts to whichever storage strategy the business needs.

items: Hexagonal layering with ports/adapters for persistence
Use-case classes that take primitive inputs and return DTOs
Repository interfaces in the domain, implementations in infrastructure
CLI commands as thin controllers over the application layer
Transactional workflows that compose multiple aggregates safely

sgci-app.text: The result is a codebase where every business rule is reachable from a single file, and every delivery adapter can be swapped without touching the domain.

campuslove.text: CampusLove was my first serious tour of PostgreSQL from the application side. Beyond the matchmaking surface, the project is a study of how to design schemas you can query fast, index thoughtfully, and migrate safely over time.

items: PostgreSQL schema design with referential integrity and indexes
Parameterized SQL queries (no string concatenation, ever)
Modular console commands split by feature
Separation between persistence models and domain shape

campuslove.text: It looks like a toy app on the outside, but it's where I internalized the habits I now rely on at work when designing production schemas.

todo-list-flask.text: I built this task-management web app with Python and Flask in March 2023. SQLite stores the task data, and PythonAnywhere hosts the application.

items: Flask routes and templates for task management
User registration, login, and per-user task lists
SQLite for persistent storage
Deployment on PythonAnywhere

todo-list-flask.text: It was an early opportunity to connect a web interface, server-side logic, persistent data, and a public deployment in one project.

formula1-webcomponents.text: The only retained frontend project in this portfolio — kept because it proves the range without leaning on a framework. Three.js does the 3D rendering, Bootstrap handles the tables and layout, and the glue is all native Web Components.

items: Team, driver, and vehicle CRUD with a reactive UI
Three.js scenes rendered on per-track circuits
Native custom elements, no framework runtime
Responsive design that holds up on phone and desktop
